chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who has his wife with him, then he remains silent and does not speak. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is he mute?' I said: 'Yes.' So it is known from him that he hates his wife and dislikes her. Is it permissible for his guardian to divorce her on his behalf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he can write it and bear witness to that.' I said: 'He cannot write nor hear, how does he divorce her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By that which is recognized from him through his actions, like what you mentioned of his dislike and hatred for her.'
ai.seo_question: How is a mute man's divorce valid if he cannot speak, write, or hear?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the mechanism of *khul'* or unilateral divorce for a mute husband who lacks the ability to speak, write, or hear. The Imam establishes that while a guardian (*wali*) cannot act on his behalf, the divorce is validly executed through distinct, observable actions (*fi'l*) that demonstrate his clear intent and aversion, thereby preserving the legal validity of the separation without requiring verbal articulation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu nasr who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have the woman with him. Then he kept silent and could not speak’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He became mute?’ I said, ‘Yes. So it was known from him to be with hatred for his wife and his abhorrence for her. Is it allowed that his guardian divorces on his behalf?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. But, he can write it out and keep witnesses upon that’. 
I said, ‘He can neither write nor hear, how would he divorce her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By that which is recognised from him from his actions the likes of what you mentioned from his abhorrence, and his hatred for her’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who is mute, does not speak and has a wife. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is he speechless?’ I replied, ‘Yes, he is speechless and it is seen that he hates his wife and dislikes her. Is it permissible for his guardian to divorce on his behalf?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not permissible, however, he can write and arrange for witnesses for it.’ I then said. ‘He cannot write or speak, how can he divorce?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It then is done by what is understood from him in the form of his deeds like what you mentioned that he hates and dislikes his wife.’”
